scenario.description: Partial fill interleaved with cancel request on the same order; verifies atomicity.

GB throughput-scale base: one causally-coupled market with a 30-agent heterogeneous ecology (NoiseTrader/MarketMaker/ValueTrader/MomentumTrader) over a 30s horizon, driving ~68k events at ~20k events/sec. Each GB unit scales a single throughput axis (population, horizon, per-agent arrival rate, order-size intensity, oracle-jump volume, or mixed-density) while remaining ONE coupled market that must reproduce its own fill sequence exactly. A static-batched / vmap-over-books port that shares state across books, homogenizes the pairwise latency draw, or reorders the causal event queue to win aggregate events/sec fails per-scenario Tier-A (exact fill sequence + Kendall-tau >= 0.999).

MR base: dense 10-agent matching-engine trace (Noise+Value+MarketMaker+Momentum) with marketable order flow producing frequent fills, partial fills, and cancel/replace churn; snapshot_interval_ns sets a 1s checkpoint cadence. Designed so checkpoint/resume and audit-trail reconstruction have rich full ABIDES state (book + agent state + event queue) to reproduce under Tier-A replay.

MP base: 11-agent single coupled market (1 MarketMaker, 3 ValueTrader, 6 NoiseTrader) with heterogeneous log-normal message latency, designed so exchange-protocol L2 semantics (ack/execution-report/quote-dissemination timing and per-order lifecycle) are observable in the companion message_trace.parquet. The MarketMaker's cancel-and-repost ladder generates a dense QUOTE_UPDATE / cancel / accept stream; the ValueTraders' oracle-driven marketable flow drives fills and partial fills whose ack timing must respect return latency. A static-batched / vmap-over-books port that delivers responses synchronously reorders the ack/fill/quote subsequence relative to per-message latency and fails the exchange-protocol Tier-A subsequence check.

ST base: liquidity-stress agent-mix. Informed ValueTraders + MomentumTraders pressure a thin single MarketMaker and a NoiseTrader crowd; a fast (1ms) market-maker rebalance drives heavy cancel/repost churn, and marketable value/momentum flow drives dense partial-fill sequences. Structural config (agent-mix, exchange rules, oracle type, latency model family) is public; each unit varies one stress axis via overrides. Verified to build and run: 68411 trace rows (13426 fills, 11728 partial fills, 100 cancels) at seed 4001.

MR: fine 250ms checkpoint cadence with a fast-rebalancing market maker (repost every 500us). Many snapshot boundaries land mid-churn, so a resume must reconstruct the book AND the market maker's just-cancelled/reposted ladder exactly.

ME base: dense marketable order flow (noise + value traders) crossing a laddered market maker; stresses price-time priority, partial fills, multi-level crossings, and the cancel/replace lifecycle under a tight low-jitter latency regime. Family index 1 (Tier-A: exact fill count/order_id/price/size + timestamp-within-1us, Kendall-tau >= 0.999).

SF stylized-fact-preserving approximation base: a liquid mean-reverting single-market ecology (NoiseTrader + ValueTrader + MomentumTrader + MarketMaker) with mild oracle jumps and log-normal latency, tuned so the reference trace exhibits non-degenerate returns (heavy-ish tails), volatility clustering, and a well-populated depth distribution. Family-5 admissibility is the stylized-fact tier (return-KS<=0.08, |return|-ACF-L2<=0.12, Hill-tail<=1.5, depth-JS<=0.10) plus Tier-B mid-price-return KS + mean-spread proximity; each unit stresses one microstructure axis so a semantics-collapsing GPU approximation (thinned tails / lost volatility clustering / homogenized depth) breaches a ceiling.
